prior_decision.quote: Consistent with the assumption of the SCT (Turner, 1991;Turner et al., 1987), participants exposed to the in-group majority showed the increase in conformity in comparison to the standard condition in which group identity was not salient. On the opposite, when the majority was presented as the out-group, the conformity effect significantly dropped. Thus, we replicated and extended past research (Abrahams et al., 1990), showing that self-categorization could play a determining role in conformity even in more minimal conditions, in which salient in-and out-group characteristics (i.e., ethnicity) were completely irrelevant for the task at hand.
prior_decision.reason: In addition to replicating the classic Asch conformity effect, the study explicitly adapts the design of Abrams et al. (1990) to re-test their finding that self-categorization (in-group vs. out-group majority membership) moderates conformity in the Asch paradigm without confounding similarity and competence (lines 6-7), and explicitly concludes that it replicated and extended Abrams et al. (1990) (line 22). This is an omitted target in the shipped dataset.

luna_triage.reason: The study describes and tests Abrams et al.’s specific finding that self-categorization/group similarity moderates conformity, then explicitly says it replicated and extended that past research. Supplied row 7 is an Asch original, a different work and finding; it does not represent Abrams et al.
